paper_title: HeLIOS: The Superfluid Helium Ultralight Dark Matter Detector
notes: This is a prototype/concept paper demonstrating the working principle of the HeLIOS detector. Figure 1 shows PROJECTED sensitivities (dashed lines for 'Optimized' future generations) for both scalar UDM (coupling d_me to electron mass) and vector UDM (coupling g_B-L to baryon-minus-lepton number) after 1 hour integration time. The paper explicitly states 'future generations of HeLIOS could explore unconstrained parameter space' and shows these as projections, not measured exclusion limits. The current prototype has NOT achieved thermal-noise-limited readout (Section IV states 'attempts to observe thermally driven motion at 20 mK temperature were unsuccessful'). No numerical data points can be reliably extracted from the figure axes without digitization, and the paper provides no tabular data. The local DM density ρ_dm = 0.4 GeV/cm³ is stated in the text as the standard halo model assumption. Two coupling types are discussed: ScalarElectron (d_me, left panel) and VectorBL (g_B-L, right panel). Since the paper discusses both equally and the extraction is from a projection plot without explicit numerical values, confidence is low. The scalar coupling is listed first in the abstract and main text discussion. | [VISION GATE A] is_projection=true but the vision notes say the traced curve is existing constraints — not the paper's own projected curve
